items.note: Field experiment randomly assigning technology-consulting employees to LLM assistance or none, with supervisor and external-evaluator creativity ratings; abstract gives no N (press reports 250); SSRN 10.2139/ssrn.5864662 is the same study; full text should check the reported later-unassisted-creativity result.
System paper (VeriForge) with a within-subjects study of 12 writers against a baseline condition; experts rated domain grounding of passages, not creativity, and N is far below 50.

Study 2 compares culturally aligned versus misaligned AI models (ChatGPT vs ErnieBot) on novelty and usefulness of creative solutions, an AI-configuration comparison; Study 1 is model-only and Study 3 is a survey field study; N (about 385 per search notes) is not in the abstract.

Classroom quasi-experiment with three middle-school classes (45, 41, 45) under computer-assisted, GenAI without supervision, and GenAI with supervision teaching; outcomes are a knowledge test, satisfaction, and engagement, with no creativity measure in the abstract despite inclusion in a creativity meta-analysis.

Between-group experiment with 202 participants: human-human dyads, human-internet, and two human-ChatGPT conditions on alternate uses, consequences, and problem-solving tasks, scored by humans and by Ocsai; random assignment not stated.

One-group pretest-posttest design: 31 undergraduates used ChatGPT for assignments over 10 weeks and took the CREA creativity test before and after; no control group and N below 50, so likely fails eligibility, possibly an after_ai before-after context item.

Quasi-experiment with 56 undergraduates in two groups, one allowed GenAI during the analytical phases before a creative task scored with a rubric; no significant difference; abstract from the Pegaso IRIS repository record, venue unknown.

81 students wrote texts alone, with Gemini (AI-only), and in hybrid collaboration under four prompt strategies; texts scored for lexical diversity and rated on quality and originality; design appears within-person with assignment and order not stated, and AI-only texts make part of it an AI-vs-human comparison.

Crowd workers on a summarization task under conditions that discourage LLM use (instructions, disabled copy-paste); secondary analysis finds LLM-using responses are higher quality but more homogeneous, though the task is not creative and the homogeneity contrast compares self-selected LLM users with non-users; borderline, possibly out.

Difference-in-differences on a matched panel of YouTube creators using the US versus Europe rollout of the AI Inspiration Tab; access raises output 4.1 percent and lowers within-creator diversity but does not raise similarity across creators.
